raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`FpmTiming` is the observer that `DeviceTimer.capture()` attaches to a forward pass so Forward Pass Metrics (FPM) can publish the first-start to last-end GPU span once every captured interval has completed. It kept a single `when_ready` callback and discarded the intervals after counting them, so a second consumer that wants per-segment GPU durations for the same forward (for example a diagnostic that sums the individual prefill/decode segment times) either overwrites FPM's listener or needs a second capture mechanism alongside the existing one.

## Modifications

Keep the existing ownership path (pending-interval counting, sealing after CPU submission, attachment to the batch result) and extend the observer instead of adding a parallel one:

- `when_ready` now accumulates listeners. All of them are invoked once, with the same span value, when the group completes; a listener registered after completion is still invoked immediately, as before.
- `FpmTiming.segments` exposes the captured intervals as a tuple of `TimingSegment(elapsed_seconds, metadata)` in submission order. It is built lazily on first read, so a span-only consumer never queries per-interval `elapsed_time()` or copies metadata. Reading it before the group is ready raises `RuntimeError`. Each segment is a frozen, slotted dataclass whose metadata is a read-only copy, so a consumer cannot mutate the timer's intervals.
- `wrap_forward_with_fpm` docstring now describes what the wrapper does rather than who installs it.

FPM's span semantics are unchanged: the enclosing span still includes gaps between segments, an empty group still reports `0.0`, and a multi-stream group still reports `None`. `DeviceTimer`, `GapTimer`, and the aggregate reporter interface and metadata are untouched; reporters registered between interval end and drain still receive pending samples.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model or kernel numerics change.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable: no additional device events, synchronization, or per-request work is added. `segments` is only built when a consumer reads it.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results).
- [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a reviewer before merging.
- [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss your PR.

Unit tests added to `test/registered/unit/observability/test_forward_pass_metrics.py` cover: a span consumer and a segment consumer sharing one pending group (two segments of 2 ms and 5 ms separated by a 2 ms gap yield a 9 ms span and a 7 ms segment sum, each listener notified exactly once and the aggregate reporter still receiving both samples); lazy, read-only segment snapshots built once; span-only consumers never touching per-segment durations; listeners registered before the group is sealed; and aggregate reporters added after interval end still receiving the captured intervals. The whole file passes locally (38 tests, 14 subtests).

+class TimingSegment:

 class FpmTiming:
     """First-start to last-end GPU span on one stream, including segment gaps."""
 
     def __init__(self):
         self.num_intervals = 0
         self._pending = 0
         self._sealed = False
-        self._callback = None
+        self._callbacks: list[Callable[[Optional[float]], None]] = []
+        self._intervals: list[_TimingInterval] = []
+        self._segments: Optional[tuple[TimingSegment, ...]] = None
         self._first_interval = None
         self._last_interval = None

+    @property
+    def segments(self) -> tuple[TimingSegment, ...]:
+        """Completed segments in submission order; read once ready.
+
+        Built on first read, so a span-only consumer never queries per-segment

+            if not self._sealed or self._pending:
+                raise RuntimeError("FpmTiming segments are read only once ready")

+                    elapsed_seconds=interval.elapsed_time() / 1000.0,
+                    metadata=MappingProxyType(dict(interval.metadata or {})),
+                )
+                for interval in self._intervals
+            )
+        return self._segments
+

+    def test_pending_group_supports_span_and_segment_consumers(self):
+        reporter = Mock()
+        timer = DeviceTimer(reporter)
+        intervals = [FakeInterval(2, ready=True), FakeInterval(5, start=4)]
+        timing = FpmTiming()
+        with patch.object(_TimingInterval, "create", side_effect=intervals):
+            with timer.capture(timing):
+                with device_timer_ctx(timer, "extend"):
+                    pass
+                with device_timer_ctx(timer, "decode"):
+                    pass
+        timing.seal()
+        publisher = _CollectingPublisher()
+        metrics = ForwardPassMetrics(worker_id="worker", counter_id=17)
+        timing.publish_when_ready(metrics, publisher)
+        segments = []
+
+        def collect_segments(_span):

+            )
+
+        timing.when_ready(collect_segments)

+        self.assertEqual(segments, [])
+
+        intervals[-1].ready = True
+        timer._report()
+        self.assertEqual(len(publisher.metrics), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(publisher.metrics[0].wall_time, 0.009)
+        self.assertEqual(publisher.metrics[0].counter_id, 17)
+        self.assertEqual(segments, [(0.002, "extend"), (0.005, "decode")])
+        self.assertEqual(sum(t for t, _ in segments), 0.007)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            reporter.call_args_list,
+            [
+                call(t=0.002, category="extend"),
+                call(t=0.005, category="decode"),
+            ],
+        )
+        timer._report()
+        self.assertEqual(len(publisher.metrics), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(len(segments), 2)
+
+    def test_segments_are_read_only_snapshots_built_once_ready(self):
+        timer = DeviceTimer()
+        interval = FakeInterval(7)
+        interval.elapsed_time = Mock(wraps=interval.elapsed_time)
+        timing = capture_timing(timer, interval)
+        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+            _ = timing.segments
+
+        interval.ready = True
+        timer._report()
+        segments = timing.segments
+        self.assertEqual(segments, timing.segments)
+        interval.elapsed_time.assert_called_once_with()
+        (segment,) = segments
+        self.assertEqual(segment.elapsed_seconds, 0.007)
+        self.assertEqual(dict(segment.metadata), {"category": "test"})
+        interval.metadata["category"] = "changed"
+        self.assertEqual(segment.metadata["category"], "test")
+        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
+            segment.metadata["category"] = "changed"
+        with self.assertRaises(AttributeError):
+            segment.elapsed_seconds = 0.0
+        self.assertFalse(hasattr(segment, "__dict__"))
+        self.assertIsInstance(segment, TimingSegment)
+
+    def test_span_only_consumers_skip_segment_durations(self):
+        timer = DeviceTimer()
+        intervals = [FakeInterval(2, ready=True), FakeInterval(5, True, start=4)]
+        for interval in intervals:
+            interval.elapsed_time = Mock(wraps=interval.elapsed_time)
+        timing = capture_timing(timer, *intervals)
+        timer._report()
+        ready = Mock()
+        timing.when_ready(ready)
+        ready.assert_called_once_with(0.009)
+        for interval in intervals:
+            interval.elapsed_time.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_completion_before_seal_keeps_all_listeners(self):
+        timer = DeviceTimer()
+        timing = FpmTiming()
+        callbacks = [Mock(), Mock(), Mock()]
+        with patch.object(
+            _TimingInterval, "create", return_value=FakeInterval(7, ready=True)
+        ):
+            with timer.capture(timing):
+                timing.when_ready(callbacks[0])
+                timing.when_ready(callbacks[1])
+                with device_timer_ctx(timer, "decode"):
+                    pass
+        callbacks[0].assert_not_called()
+        callbacks[1].assert_not_called()
+        timing.seal()
+        timing.when_ready(callbacks[2])
+        timing.seal()
+        timer._report()
+        for callback in callbacks:
+            callback.assert_called_once_with(0.007)
+
+    def test_captured_intervals_still_reach_late_aggregate_reporters(self):
+        original, late = Mock(), Mock()
+        timer = DeviceTimer(original)
+        interval = FakeInterval(7)
+        timing = capture_timing(timer, interval)
+        interval.ready = True
+        timer.add_reporter(late)
+        timer._report()
+        for reporter in (original, late):
+            reporter.assert_called_once_with(t=0.007, category="test")
+        ready = Mock()
+        timing.when_ready(ready)
+        ready.assert_called_once_with(0.007)
+
